rationale: The assistant immediately identified the clock/AUTO lockout after a power interruption as the likely simple cause, asked the right first questions (display lit or dead, electric or gas) and, once told 'flashing 0.00' and a power cut, correctly diagnosed it without false certainty ('most likely'). It gave generic but appropriately hedged Neff clock-setting steps when the customer had no manual, warned against isolating at the wall as a reset, recommended no parts and no premature engineer call, and the customer confirmed the oven heated. Safety guidance was proportionate (no panels or wiring; engineer only if a breaker keeps tripping). Matches the hidden truth exactly.
